chunks: And with the first chain of transmission, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام:
“Indeed, 'Ali عليه السلام performed masḥ over the two sandals and did not pass underneath the two straps.”
That means when they are of the Arabian type, because they do not prevent the water from reaching the foot to the extent upon which masḥ is obligatory.

key_terms.النَّعْلَيْنِ: the two sandals worn on the feet
key_terms.الْمَسْحُ: wiping in wudu (ablution), especially over the feet
key_terms.عَرَبِيَّيْنِ: of the Arabian type, referring to a kind of sandal design
key_terms.وُصُولِ الْمَاءِ: the reaching of water to the required area

ai.seo_question: Is masḥ valid in wudu (ablution) while wearing sandals?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling related to wudu (ablution), specifically the validity of masḥ over feet while wearing certain sandals. It indicates that if the sandals are of a type that does not block access to the part of the foot requiring masḥ, the masḥ remains valid.
